_about: Development set for tuning. 20 scam + 20 normal call transcripts. Written independently of the test sets.

items.label: scam
items.type: grandchild arrested, needs bail via gift cards
items.text:
Caller: Grandpa? It's me, it's your grandson.
You: Tyler? You sound different, are you okay?
Caller: I got a cold and I, um, I got arrested. There was an accident and they found stuff in the other guy's car.
You: Oh my goodness. What do you need?
Caller: Bail is two thousand dollars and the lawyer says I can pay it with Google Play gift cards. Please don't tell Mom and Dad, they'll kill me.
You: Gift cards for bail? That seems strange.
Caller: It's how they do it here, Grandpa, I need it right now before they move me. Please, you're the only one I can call.

items.label: scam
items.type: fake bank fraud dept, move money to safe account
items.text:
Caller: Hello, this is Mark from the fraud department at Harbor Trust Bank. We've detected suspicious activity on your checking account.
You: Oh no, what kind of activity?
Caller: Someone is trying to withdraw $4,800 from a branch in Ohio. To protect your funds we need to transfer your balance into a secure safe account immediately.
You: Can't you just freeze it?
Caller: The thief has access to your online login, so freezing won't stop it. I'll give you the new account number and you'll wire the money today.
You: I'd rather go to my branch.
Caller: There's no time for that, ma'am, the money will be gone within the hour. Stay on the line with me.

items.label: scam
items.type: IRS impersonation, arrest threat
items.text:
Caller: This is Officer Daniels with the Internal Revenue Service. There is a warrant out for your arrest for unpaid back taxes.
You: A warrant? I've always paid my taxes.
Caller: Our records show you owe $6,240 from 2023. If you don't settle today, local police will come to your home this afternoon.
You: How do I pay it?
Caller: You'll need to go to the store and buy prepaid cards, then read me the numbers on the back. Do not hang up and do not speak to anyone at the store about this.
You: I think I should call my accountant.
Caller: If you hang up the warrant goes into effect immediately.

items.label: scam
items.type: Social Security number suspended
items.text:
Caller: This is an urgent message from the Social Security Administration. Your Social Security number has been suspended due to suspicious activity.
You: Suspended? What does that mean?
Caller: Your number was used in a crime in Texas. To reactivate it I need to verify your full SSN and your date of birth.
You: I don't feel comfortable giving that out.
Caller: Ma'am, if you don't verify now your benefits will be stopped and your bank accounts will be frozen.
You: My benefits? I live on those.
Caller: Then let's fix it right now. Please read me your number.

items.label: scam
items.type: tech support, remote access and refund
items.text:
Caller: Hi, I'm calling from Microsoft technical support. Your computer has been sending us error messages, it's infected with a virus.
You: Really? It has been running slow.
Caller: Yes, hackers are getting into it. I need you to go to a website and download a program so I can connect and fix it.
You: Okay, I'm at the computer now.
Caller: Good. After I clean it there's a $299 service fee, and you can pay with Bitcoin at the machine at your local store.
You: Bitcoin? I don't know how to do that.
Caller: I'll walk you through it, just don't turn off the computer.

items.label: scam
items.type: power company shut-off threat
items.text:
Caller: This is the disconnection department at Valley Electric. Your power is scheduled to be shut off in 45 minutes for non-payment.
You: But I paid my bill last week.
Caller: We have no record of that payment. To avoid disconnection you need to pay $512 right now.
You: It's freezing out, I can't lose the heat.
Caller: Then you need to act immediately. We accept payment through Zelle or a prepaid card.
You: Can I call the number on my bill?
Caller: If you hang up, the technician is already on the way and the shut-off will go ahead.

items.label: scam
items.type: prize or lottery processing fee
items.text:
Caller: Congratulations! You've been selected as the second-place winner of the National Sweepstakes, a prize of two hundred fifty thousand dollars and a new car.
You: Oh my, I don't remember entering anything.
Caller: Your name was entered through a store purchase. All you need to do is cover the taxes and processing fee of $1,900.
You: Can't you take it out of the winnings?
Caller: By federal law the fee has to be paid up front. You can send it by Western Union today.
You: Hmm, let me think.
Caller: The offer expires at five o'clock, and please keep this confidential until the prize is delivered.

items.label: scam
items.type: online romance asking for money
items.text:
Caller: Hello my darling, it's Richard. I've missed hearing your voice.
You: Richard! I thought you were on the oil rig.
Caller: I am, sweetheart, but there's a problem. My bank account is frozen and I need to pay the customs on my equipment.
You: Oh no, how much is it?
Caller: Only three thousand five hundred dollars, and then I can finally fly to meet you. You can send it in Bitcoin, I'll text you the address.
You: My daughter says I should be careful with money.
Caller: Please don't tell her, she doesn't understand what we have. I'll pay you back the moment I land.

items.label: scam
items.type: crypto investment opportunity
items.text:
Caller: Good afternoon, I'm with Summit Digital Assets. We help retirees grow their savings with cryptocurrency.
You: I'm not really into that stuff.
Caller: I understand, but our clients are seeing returns of 30 percent a month, guaranteed. It's completely safe.
You: Guaranteed? Nothing is guaranteed.
Caller: This one is. If you transfer ten thousand dollars from your IRA today, I'll set up your account personally.
You: I'd want to talk to my financial advisor first.
Caller: Advisors don't like this because it cuts into their fees. The window closes tonight, so we really need to move now.

items.label: scam
items.type: fake disaster charity
items.text:
Caller: Hi, I'm calling for the Gulf Coast Hurricane Relief Fund. Families lost everything in last week's storm.
You: Oh, that's terrible, I saw it on the news.
Caller: We're trying to get food and water there today. Could you give a donation of two hundred dollars?
You: Can you send me something in the mail?
Caller: There's no time for mail, people are suffering right now. You can give it over the phone with a gift card or wire it to our relief account.
You: I usually give through my church.
Caller: Every hour counts, ma'am. Even fifty dollars in a gift card would help.

items.label: scam
items.type: delivery or customs fee
items.text:
Caller: This is the customs office at the international shipping center. We are holding a package addressed to you.
You: A package? From who?
Caller: It was sent from overseas and there's an import fee of $89 before we can release it. If it's not paid today it will be returned and you'll be charged a penalty.
You: I'm not expecting anything.
Caller: It may be a gift. Just give me your card number and the expiration date and I'll process the fee.
You: I don't give my card out over the phone.
Caller: Then you can pay with an Apple gift card, just read me the code.

items.label: scam
items.type: virtual kidnapping ransom
items.text:
Caller: Listen to me carefully. I have your daughter. If you want to see her again, you will do exactly what I say.
You: What? Where is she? Let me talk to her!
Caller: She's crying, she can't talk. You will get fifteen thousand dollars and send it by wire. Do not call the police.
You: Please don't hurt her.
Caller: Stay on the line. Do not hang up, do not text anyone. If you hang up, she is gone.
You: I don't have that kind of money.
Caller: Then get what you can, right now. Go to the bank and don't tell them why.

items.label: scam
items.type: fake lawyer recovering earlier scam losses
items.text:
Caller: Hello, I'm attorney Steven Clark with the Fraud Recovery Group. Our records show you lost money to a sweepstakes scam last year.
You: Yes, I did. I lost almost a thousand dollars.
Caller: Good news, we've recovered your funds, seven thousand two hundred dollars including damages.
You: Really? That's wonderful.
Caller: There is just a legal filing fee of $600 to release the money. You can wire it to our escrow account today.
You: Why would I pay to get my own money back?
Caller: It's a court requirement, ma'am. If we don't receive it by tomorrow the funds go back to the state.

items.label: scam
items.type: Medicare impersonation asking for ID number
items.text:
Caller: Hi, this is Linda from Medicare. We're issuing new plastic Medicare cards with a chip and yours is ready to ship.
You: Oh, I didn't know they were changing them.
Caller: Yes, but your old card will be cancelled tomorrow. I just need to verify your Medicare number and your bank account for the processing fee.
You: There's a fee?
Caller: Only $35, and it's taken right from your account. Can you read me the number on your current card?
You: I'll call the number on my card first.
Caller: If you hang up we can't guarantee your coverage, you could lose your benefits.

items.label: scam
items.type: subtle: move savings to protected account
items.text:
Caller: Good morning, this is Karen in the account security office at First Meridian. I'm calling about a change on your savings account.
You: Oh, is something wrong?
Caller: We noticed a login from a new device, and as a precaution we're helping customers move their balance into a protected account while we investigate.
You: How does that work?
Caller: I'll stay with you while you open the app and transfer the full balance to the account details I give you. It's only temporary, it comes back once things are cleared.
You: Should I go into the branch instead?
Caller: I'd keep it between us for now, ma'am, some branch staff may be involved. Let's just take care of it together on this call.

items.label: scam
items.type: subtle: grandchild trouble, cashier's check and courier pickup
items.text:
Caller: Hi Grandma, it's me. I'm okay, but I'm kind of in a mess.
You: Sweetheart, what happened?
Caller: I had a fender bender and the other driver is really upset. My attorney says if we settle it quietly it won't go on my record.
You: Well, how much would that be?
Caller: About eight thousand five hundred. He says the easiest way is a cashier's check, and someone from his office can come by the house this afternoon to pick it up.
You: Shouldn't I call your father?
Caller: Please, Grandma, I'm so embarrassed. Let's just handle it between us, I'll explain everything at Thanksgiving.

items.label: scam
items.type: subtle: fake internet provider has user install app
items.text:
Caller: Hi, this is Jason from Lakeside Internet. We're seeing some unusual traffic coming from your home network.
You: Oh dear, is that bad?
Caller: It might mean someone is using your connection. I can check it from here if you install a small app called QuickAssist Pro from the app store.
You: Okay, it's downloading now.
Caller: Great. When it opens it will show a nine-digit number, just read that to me and accept the connection.
You: Alright, it says four two seven, eight one...
Caller: Perfect. Now while I'm checking, go ahead and log in to your bank so I can make sure nobody has touched it.

items.label: scam
items.type: subtle: caller asks to read a code from a text
items.text:
Caller: Hi there, this is Andrea from Northgate Bank's customer care team. We're just confirming a recent update to your profile.
You: I didn't update anything.
Caller: That's exactly why I'm calling. To cancel the change I'm going to send a confirmation message to your phone.
You: Okay, I just got a text.
Caller: Wonderful. Could you read me the six numbers in that message so I can reverse the update?
You: The text says not to share it with anyone.
Caller: That's just a standard line, since I'm with the bank it's fine. It's only so I can stop the change for you.

items.label: scam
items.type: subtle: missed jury duty, pay fine in cash to courier
items.text:
Caller: Good afternoon, this is Sergeant Hall with the county sheriff's office. You were summoned for jury service last month and didn't appear.
You: I never got a summons.
Caller: It was mailed to your address, and the judge has issued a citation. We can resolve it today with a bond of $1,500.
You: How would I even do that?
Caller: Withdraw it in cash and one of our deputies will meet you outside the bank to collect it and give you a receipt.
You: That seems unusual.
Caller: It's a sensitive matter, so I'd advise you not to discuss it with family to avoid any embarrassment. Keep your phone with you until the deputy arrives.

items.label: scam
items.type: subtle: landlord or contractor changing payment details
items.text:
Caller: Hi, this is Greg from Oak Ridge Property Management. Quick heads up about your rent this month.
You: Hi Greg, is everything alright?
Caller: Yes, we've switched banks, so this month's payment needs to go to our new account. I'll send you the routing and account numbers.
You: I usually just mail a check to the office.
Caller: The office is closed for renovations, so checks would be delayed and late fees would apply. Please send the transfer by Friday.
You: Can I get that in writing from the owner?
Caller: He's traveling, but I'm handling everything. Just use the new details and don't use the old address anymore.

items.label: normal
items.type: daughter checking in
items.text:
Caller: Hi Mom, just calling to see how your week's going.
You: Oh hi honey. Pretty good, I went to the garden club on Tuesday.
Caller: That's nice. Did they get the new benches put in?
You: They did, they look lovely. How are the kids?
Caller: Busy, Emma has a soccer game Saturday if you want to come.
You: I'd love that. What time?
Caller: Ten o'clock, I can pick you up around nine thirty.

items.label: normal
items.type: pharmacy refill ready
items.text:
Caller: Hi, this is Maria at Elm Street Pharmacy. Your blood pressure prescription is ready for pickup.
You: Oh good, I was just about out.
Caller: We're open until eight tonight, and the drive-through is open too.
You: Do I owe anything this time?
Caller: Your copay is ten dollars, same as last month. You can pay when you pick it up.
You: Great, I'll come by this afternoon. Thank you.

items.label: normal
items.type: dentist appointment reminder
items.text:
Caller: Hello, this is Jenny from Brightside Dental calling to remind you of your cleaning tomorrow at 2:30.
You: Oh, thank you, I almost forgot.
Caller: No problem. Please arrive ten minutes early and bring your insurance card.
You: Will do. Is Dr. Patel still seeing me?
Caller: Yes, she is. If you need to reschedule, just call the office.
You: No, tomorrow works. See you then.

items.label: normal
items.type: friend with exciting news
items.text:
Caller: Barbara, you'll never guess what happened!
You: Carol! What is it?
Caller: My son and his wife are having twins! They just found out this morning.
You: Oh, how wonderful, congratulations!
Caller: I'm already planning to knit two of everything. Can you believe it?
You: You'll have your hands full. We should celebrate at lunch on Thursday.
Caller: Yes, let's do the café by the library, my treat.

items.label: normal
items.type: neighbor holding a package
items.text:
Caller: Hi, it's Dave from next door. The mail carrier left one of your packages on my porch by mistake.
You: Oh, thanks Dave. I've been waiting for that.
Caller: I'll bring it over after dinner if that's okay.
You: That's perfect. How's your hip doing?
Caller: Getting better, physical therapy is helping. I'll see you around seven.
You: Sounds good, I'll leave the porch light on.

items.label: normal
items.type: doctor's office with test results
items.text:
Caller: Hi, this is Nurse Angela from Dr. Reyes's office. I'm calling with your lab results from last week.
You: Oh, okay, is everything alright?
Caller: Everything looks good. Your cholesterol came down a little since last time.
You: That's a relief, I've been walking every morning.
Caller: It shows. The doctor would like to see you again in six months, we'll send a reminder card.
You: Thank you so much for letting me know.

items.label: normal
items.type: furniture delivery driver
items.text:
Caller: Hi, this is the driver from Hometown Furniture. I've got your recliner on the truck and I'm about twenty minutes out.
You: Oh wonderful. I'll be home.
Caller: Is there a side door or should we come through the front?
You: The front is easiest, there's only two steps.
Caller: Great, we'll set it up and take the packaging with us.
You: Thank you, see you soon.

items.label: normal
items.type: church volunteer scheduling
items.text:
Caller: Hi Ruth, it's Pam from St. Mark's. We're putting together the volunteer schedule for the bake sale.
You: Oh yes, I'd like to help again this year.
Caller: Wonderful. Could you bring two pies and help at the table Saturday morning?
You: Sure, I'll make my apple pie and maybe a pumpkin.
Caller: Everyone loves your apple pie. We'll start setting up at eight.
You: I'll be there. Thanks for organizing, Pam.

items.label: normal
items.type: son planning Sunday dinner
items.text:
Caller: Hey Dad, are we still on for dinner Sunday?
You: Of course. I was thinking of making pot roast.
Caller: Sounds great. Should I bring anything?
You: Maybe some rolls and a salad.
Caller: Will do. Oh, and I'll take a look at that leaky faucet while I'm there.
You: That would be a big help. See you around five.

items.label: normal
items.type: library hold ready
items.text:
Caller: Hello, this is the Riverside Public Library. The book you put on hold has come in.
You: Oh, the new mystery novel?
Caller: Yes, that's the one. We'll hold it at the front desk for seven days.
You: I'll stop by tomorrow morning.
Caller: Great, just bring your library card. Have a nice day.
You: You too, thank you.

items.label: normal
items.type: charity mentioning mailed envelope only
items.text:
Caller: Hi, I'm a volunteer with the Countryside Animal Shelter. We're calling to thank past supporters.
You: Oh, I remember, I gave last spring.
Caller: Thank you so much. We just wanted to let you know our fall newsletter will arrive in the mail next week with a return envelope.
You: Do I need to do anything now?
Caller: Not at all, we don't take donations over the phone. If you'd like to give, the envelope or our website is the way to do it.
You: That's good to know. I'll look for it.

items.label: normal
items.type: hard negative: grandson asks for a little money in an ordinary way
items.text:
Caller: Hi Grandma, it's me, Josh. How are you doing?
You: Josh! I'm good, sweetie, how's school?
Caller: Good, midterms are done. Hey, I was wondering, could I borrow like forty dollars for my textbook? Mom said to ask you since you offered.
You: Of course. Do you want me to just give it to you at dinner Sunday?
Caller: That's perfect, no rush at all. Mom and Dad are coming too.
You: Wonderful, I'll make your favorite lasagna.
Caller: Thanks Grandma, love you. See you Sunday.

items.label: normal
items.type: hard negative: real bank fraud alert, no codes or money asked
items.text:
Caller: This is an automated fraud alert from Harbor Trust Bank. We noticed a charge of $412 at an electronics store on your debit card.
You: Hmm, I didn't buy anything like that.
Caller: If you did not make this purchase, please hang up and call the number on the back of your card. We will never ask for your PIN or a verification code.
You: Okay, I'll do that.
Caller: Your card has been temporarily locked for your protection. You can also visit any branch with photo ID.
You: Alright, I'll call them right now from the number on my card.

items.label: normal
items.type: hard negative: real police community event
items.text:
Caller: Hi, this is Officer Brooks with the Millbrook Police Department. We're calling seniors in the neighborhood about our Coffee with a Cop event.
You: Police? Is something wrong?
Caller: No, nothing's wrong at all. It's this Saturday at the community center, free coffee and donuts, and we'll talk about how to spot phone scams.
You: Oh, that sounds useful. Do I need to sign up?
Caller: No sign-up and no cost, just come by between nine and eleven. There will be a flyer at the library too.
You: I'll bring my neighbor. Thank you, officer.

items.label: normal
items.type: hard negative: user called customer service and reads code they requested
items.text:
You: Hi, I'm calling because I can't log in to my account on your website.
Caller: I'm sorry about that. I can help. Since you called us, I'll send a one-time code to the phone number on file to verify it's you.
You: Okay, I just got it. It's 5 8 2 1 9 0.
Caller: Thank you, you're verified. It looks like your password was locked after a few tries. I've sent a reset link to your email.
You: Oh, I see it. Let me try that.
Caller: Take your time. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
You: No, that's it. Thanks for your help.

items.label: normal
items.type: hard negative: don't tell anyone about the surprise party
items.text:
Caller: Hi Aunt Linda, it's Megan. I need your help with something, but don't tell anyone, okay?
You: Oh, now I'm curious. What is it?
Caller: We're throwing a surprise party for Uncle Jim's seventieth. Keep it a secret, he can't find out!
You: Oh how fun! When is it?
Caller: Saturday the 24th at our house. Could you get him there by six without spilling the beans?
You: I'll tell him we're going out for dinner. Do you need me to bring anything?
Caller: Maybe your deviled eggs. Thank you, this is going to be so great.

items.label: normal
items.type: hard negative: urgent pharmacy call about medication interaction
items.text:
Caller: Hi, this is Tom, the pharmacist at Elm Street Pharmacy. It's a little urgent, so I wanted to call you right away.
You: Oh, what's going on?
Caller: Your new antibiotic can interact with your blood thinner. Please don't start it until we talk to your doctor.
You: I was going to take the first one tonight.
Caller: Let's hold off. I've already left a message for Dr. Reyes and we'll call you back this afternoon with what to do.
You: Thank you for catching that, I appreciate it.

items.label: normal
items.type: hard negative: sister says it's me, new phone
items.text:
Caller: Hey, it's me! I got a new phone so the number's different.
You: Joan? Oh, I didn't recognize the number.
Caller: Yep, finally gave up the flip phone. Save this one, okay?
You: I will. So how was the cruise?
Caller: Oh, it was beautiful. I'll bring the photos when I visit next month.
You: I can't wait. Give my love to Frank.
Caller: I will. Talk to you Sunday like usual.

items.label: normal
items.type: hard negative: fire department free smoke detector program
items.text:
Caller: Hello, this is Lieutenant Ortiz with the Cedar Falls Fire Department. You signed up at the senior center for our free smoke detector check.
You: Oh yes, I did put my name down.
Caller: We have firefighters in your area next Tuesday morning. Would ten o'clock work?
You: That's fine. Is there any cost?
Caller: None at all, the program is free. They'll come in a marked fire truck and in uniform, and they'll test and replace batteries.
You: Great, I'll be home. Thank you.

items.label: normal
items.type: hard negative: grandson's news mentions bank, money and police
items.text:
Caller: Grandpa, it's me, Kevin! I've got big news, I got the job at the bank!
You: Kevin, that's great! The one downtown?
Caller: Yeah, I start in two weeks as a teller. The money's way better than the restaurant.
You: I'm proud of you. Your grandma would have been thrilled.
Caller: Thanks. Oh, and funny thing, the background check made me go down to the police station for fingerprints.
You: That's normal for banks, they're careful. Let's go out to lunch to celebrate.
Caller: Definitely. I'll call you this weekend to pick a day.
